Package org.apache.juneau.commons.concurrent

Interface ReplayCache

All Known Implementing Classes:
InMemoryReplayCache
public interface ReplayCache
SPI for detecting reuse ("replay") of a one-time-use identifier.

A consumer wires a ReplayCache to narrow a token/identifier that would otherwise be usable any number of times within its lifetime down to single-use: the second and every subsequent submission of the same identifier is reported as a replay. The SPI is deliberately generic — it deals only in a String identifier and a long absolute expiry, with no dependency on any particular protocol or transport.

Atomic check-and-record (no TOCTOU). checkAndRecord(String, long) both checks whether an identifier has been seen before and records it as seen, as one indivisible operation. A separate "seen" followed by a separate "record" would leave a race window in which two near-simultaneous submissions of the same identifier could both observe "not yet seen" and both proceed; implementations must guarantee that of any two concurrent calls with the same identifier, at most one returns true.

Fail-mode is a consumer decision. When the backing store cannot answer — for example a remote store is unreachable — an implementation may either throw or return an outcome. The consumer decides how a thrown failure is resolved by passing a ReplayCache.FailMode to checkAndRecord(String, long, FailMode, Consumer):

  • ReplayCache.FailMode.FAIL_CLOSED (the safe default) treats a store failure as a replay (reject).
  • ReplayCache.FailMode.FAIL_OPEN treats a store failure as first-seen (allow), degrading to the multi-use-tolerant behavior a consumer would have with no ReplayCache wired at all.
An implementation that wants to enforce its own outcome on store failure (rather than defer to the consumer's ReplayCache.FailMode) can catch its own failures internally and return true/false from checkAndRecord(String, long) instead of throwing.

The built-in default is per-process only. The zero-config built-in implementation (InMemoryReplayCache) is backed by process-local memory, so it only enforces single-use within one process. Cross-node single-use requires a consumer-supplied ReplayCache backed by a store shared across every node.

  • Method Details

    • checkAndRecord

      boolean checkAndRecord(String id, long expiresAtMs)
      Atomically checks whether the specified identifier has been observed before and records it as seen if not.

      Implementations own their own timeout. A call that blocks indefinitely (for example a remote store with no client-side deadline) blocks the caller with it. An implementation backed by a network store must bound its own call so a slow/unreachable backend surfaces promptly as a throw (which the caller resolves per its chosen ReplayCache.FailMode) or a return, never an unbounded stall.

      Parameters:
      id - The identifier to check. Never null.
      expiresAtMs - The identifier's own absolute expiry, in epoch milliseconds. An implementation may use this to self-evict a record once it can no longer matter.
      Returns:
      true if this is the first time the identifier has been observed (the caller should proceed); false if it has been observed before (the caller should reject the submission as a replay).

    • checkAndRecord

      default boolean checkAndRecord(String id, long expiresAtMs, ReplayCache.FailMode failMode)
      Invokes checkAndRecord(String, long) applying the specified fail-mode policy on a thrown failure.

      Equivalent to checkAndRecord(id, expiresAtMs, failMode, null).

      Parameters:
      id - The identifier to check. Never null.
      expiresAtMs - The identifier's own absolute expiry, in epoch milliseconds.
      failMode - The policy to apply if checkAndRecord(String, long) throws. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      true if the caller should proceed; false if the submission should be rejected.

    • checkAndRecord

      default boolean checkAndRecord(String id, long expiresAtMs, ReplayCache.FailMode failMode, Consumer<Exception> onFailure)
      Invokes checkAndRecord(String, long) applying the specified fail-mode policy on a thrown failure.

      If checkAndRecord(String, long) throws, the exception is passed to onFailure (when non-null) and then resolved to true for ReplayCache.FailMode.FAIL_OPEN or false for ReplayCache.FailMode.FAIL_CLOSED.

      Parameters:
      id - The identifier to check. Never null.
      expiresAtMs - The identifier's own absolute expiry, in epoch milliseconds.
      failMode - The policy to apply if checkAndRecord(String, long) throws. Must not be null.
      onFailure - A handler invoked with the thrown exception before the policy is applied. Can be null.
      Returns:
      true if the caller should proceed; false if the submission should be rejected.
